title: Chapter 42
content:
Kang Il-hyun summoned a staff member to order fresh tea, then settled back to watch Jakyeong eat.

It was well before normal working hours were over—why had he returned so early? The constant proximity was suffocating. Jakyeong wanted nothing more than to finish the food and retreat upstairs. As his pace picked up, Il-hyun watched with an amused smirk.

"Take your time. Didn't you get enough to eat last night?"

Jakyeong’s eyes narrowed into sharp daggers. Il-hyun chuckled, waving a hand to urge him to keep eating. Jakyeong chewed carefully, but the steak felt like it was sticking in his throat. Setting his fork down, he dabbed his mouth with a napkin.

Il-hyun crossed his forearms over the table, leaning in slightly.

"There's something I'm curious about."

Jakyeong raised an eyebrow.

"Why did you kill Choi Moon-sung?"

The abrupt mention of the name caught Jakyeong off guard. He kept his expression neutral. "Who is that?"

Il-hyun let out an appreciative chuckle, as if watching a precocious child play dumb. "Come now. You killed him yourself. Choi Ki-tae’s father."

"I didn't kill anyone."

"A personal vendetta?"

"I told you, it wasn't me."

"Definitely a vendetta," Il-hyun concluded smoothly. "So that leaves only Choi Ki-tae, doesn't it?"

Jakyeong kept silent. He had every intention of eliminating Ki-tae when the right window opened, but volunteering that information was unnecessary. An outsider might wonder why the sons had to die alongside the father, but leaving surviving bloodlines was an invitation for future retribution. After all, wasn't Jakyeong living proof of that exact threat?

"How did you take him out? A bullet? Or a blade?"

Il-hyun propped his chin on his palm, wearing a look of genuine fascination. Jakyeong maintained a wall of complete ignorance.

"Word is his face was pulverized beyond recognition."

"..."

"You can't do that to me."

Il-hyun tapped his own left chest with his index finger.

"Shoot right here. Here. Don't go putting a stray round in the wrong spot and sending me straight to the grave."

Is he actually getting nervous about catching a bullet? Looking at that arrogant face, one would think he'd laugh even if a cannon shell were flying straight at his skull.

Jakyeong reached across the table, taking Il-hyun's fingers and shifting them slightly toward the center-right.

Most people assumed the heart was situated squarely on the left, but anatomically, it sat in the central mediastinum, angled slightly leftward. When executing a center-mass sniper shot, aiming slightly inward ensured the round wouldn't drift off-target.

"The heart is here."

Il-hyun held his gaze, his lips curving upward. "Look at that. How thoughtful. Would you like to show me where my cock is with your hands, too?"

Jakyeong’s face instantly twisted into pure disgust.

Maybe I should put the round straight through his groin instead. A lifetime of forced celibacy seemed like fitting karma. Just visualizing it brought a small, involuntary smirk to his lips. He quickly suppressed it, putting on a polished, professional facade.

"Don't worry, Director Kang. That won't be necessary."

Jakyeong picked up a slice of watermelon from the fruit platter. Chewing the sweet flesh, he looked for somewhere to dispose of the seeds.

Noticing the pause, Il-hyun held out an open palm across the table. Spit them here.

Jakyeong’s first instinct was to spit them straight into the man's smug face, but he checked the urge, letting the black seeds fall onto the stone patio instead.

"Spit them there, and watermelons are going to sprout all over the yard."

"How wonderful. You can harvest them yourself next summer... assuming you're still breathing by then."

Il-hyun’s eyes crinkled with genuine delight at the jab. "Such lovely words from such a handsome face. A treat to listen to."

Ignoring the flattery, Jakyeong finished the fruit in silence. He stacked the plates and empty glasses neatly onto the silver service tray. Lingering out here would only spike his blood pressure; slipping upstairs to rest was the priority.

As he stood up with the tray, Il-hyun watched him with chin in hand.

"Want me to kill him for you?"

Jakyeong paused, looking down at him.

"Choi Ki-tae. Shall I put him in the ground for you?"

The smile remained on Il-hyun's lips, but the warmth in his eyes had turned razor-sharp.

Meeting that dark gaze, Jakyeong offered a thin, mocking smile of his own. "I would certainly appreciate the gesture."

With a polite nod, Jakyeong carried the tray inside. Glancing back through the floor-to-ceiling glass, Il-hyun was still sitting in the afternoon breeze, quietly sipping his tea.

The housekeeper emerged from the prep kitchen, taking the tray from his hands. "Leave these tasks to the domestic staff, Young Master. You shouldn't be clearing tables yourself."

"It's no trouble at all. Thank you for the meal—I'll head up to rest now."

He turned toward the stairs, but she caught his elbow. "Young Master Yi-an, the Director brought back a gift for you."

Jakyeong’s brow furrowed. Normally, receiving a gift was pleasant, but accepting anything from Kang Il-hyun—aside from cold, untraceable cash—sounded like a terrible idea.

Noticing his reluctance, she guided him toward the living room sofa anyway. Resting on the cushion was an elegant gift box, wrapped in soft pastel paper, tied with an elaborate silk ribbon, and finished with a fresh floral corsage.

"Is... that it?"

"Yes. Take it upstairs and open it."

She beamed with maternal pride, as if she had received the parcel herself. To her, seeing the notoriously cold and detached second son bring home a beautifully wrapped gift for a houseguest was a heartwarming milestone.

Jakyeong lifted the parcel with cautious reluctance. It was surprisingly heavy—roughly nine or ten pounds.

He carried it up to his second-floor suite and set it down on the coffee table. He slipped off the ribbon and pulled the lid back.

A sharp, metallic stench of iron and blood hit his nostrils instantly.

Jakyeong froze. No way... Surely not...

He lifted the inner wrapping and removed the lid entirely. His face went cold.

Black hair spilled across the base of the box, framing blood-spattered lashes and the bridge of a nose.

Resting inside was the severed head of Choi Ki-tae.

Judging by the way the skin along the severed neck had contracted and curled, the blade had carved through the tissue while the man was still breathing.

Jakyeong looked through the window; Kang Il-hyun was still lounging casually on the patio below. Replacing the cardboard lid, Jakyeong picked up the box and walked back downstairs.

He strode across the lawn, setting the heavy parcel squarely onto the glass table before Il-hyun.

"What is the meaning of this?"

"You said you'd appreciate it if I killed him."

"..."

A chill passed through the air as Il-hyun looked up at him. "What's that face for? Are you feeling sentimental now that he's dead?"

Jakyeong felt no pity, but showing a shred of remorse right now looked like a fast track to having his own head boxed up. He moved to pick the parcel back up to incinerate or bury the remains.

"Where are you taking it?"

"You said it was a gift. Now that it's in my possession, what I do with it is my business."

"Don't tell me you're planning to cradle it and weep?"

The mocking drawl was icy.

Why had he murdered Choi Ki-tae? Because the death of the patriarch rendered the son useless to the syndicate? Or because the man had dared to leave a bruise on Jakyeong's throat? Given Il-hyun's deranged patterns, the latter was absurdly plausible.

Did Ki-tae ever imagine that a single drunken advance at a private villa would cost him his head?

Jakyeong had crossed paths with enough sociopaths to know how their minds worked. They treated human lives like disposable playthings, yet harbored a psychotic hatred for anyone else laying a finger on their property. But that possessive mania was always fleeting. Once the novelty wore off, their cruelty turned inward. Next time, it could very well be Jakyeong's severed head inside a pastel box.

"I'm going to bury it. Leaving it out where the staff might see serves no purpose."

Il-hyun let out a sharp, piercing whistle.

From behind the estate villas, a dark shape tore across the turf at breakneck speed. It was the German Shepherd that had cornered Jakyeong days ago.

While Jakyeong’s attention was diverted, Il-hyun grabbed the box, seized the severed head by its matted hair, and hurled it onto the open grass.

Jakyeong caught a glimpse of Ki-tae's face. The nose and eyes were intact, but the lips and jaw had been systematically pulverized into a mangled, unrecognizable pulp of flesh and bone.

The attack dog clamped its jaws onto the hair and dragged the gory prize back into the woods. In a matter of seconds, the head was gone.

"There. No need to dig a hole, is there?"

Looking at Il-hyun's bright, charming smile, Jakyeong was left completely speechless.

Emerging from the shower, Jakyeong dried off, pulled on a pair of cotton briefs, and stood before the vanity mirror.

Squeezing a generous dollop of medicinal ointment onto his fingertip, he smoothed it over his bruised chest. His nipples were raw and inflamed from being sucked and bitten, stinging fiercely whenever fabric brushed against them.

Cursing under his breath, he applied ointment to the other side, letting out a bitter, self-deprecating laugh at his reflection. The touch sent a strange, electric thrum through his nerves. He had spent his entire life believing his only erogenous zone was his groin—because that was the only place that had ever brought physical release.

Yet last night... The unbidden memory of Kang Il-hyun driving into him from behind while whispering filth flashed violently in his mind.

Jakyeong shook his head furiously, dispelling the image. Looking down at the swollen tissue with a tired sigh, he pulled a clean shirt over his shoulders.

Seven days left until the inauguration. Seven days, and this nightmare would be finished. Until then, avoiding any further contact with Kang Il-hyun was the only survival strategy that mattered.

He stepped into the lounge, turned the climate control down, and pulled a yoga mat from the cabinet. Rolling it out before the window, he settled into a cross-legged meditative pose. He started an ambient track—the soft trickle of water layered with the deep resonance of Tibetan singing bowls gradually quieted his chaotic thoughts.

Drawing a slow, deep breath, he exhaled the tension in a long, controlled stream, methodically scrubbing the violence of the past few days from his mind. The subtle vibrational hum traveled through his nerves, releasing the locked tension in his muscles.

["Look at whose cock you're taking right now."]

His brow furrowed tightly behind closed lids. The memory of Il-hyun panting heavily over his shoulder forced its way back into his consciousness like an intrusive specter.

Jakyeong snapped his eyes open, killing the track with a sharp tap.

"Fuck..."

Pushing himself up from the mat, a phone began buzzing on the sofa.

He picked up the burner device. An unfamiliar number was flashing across the screen. Only three people had access to this line: Kang Il-hyun, Kang Seok-joo, and the late Choi Ki-tae.

With Ki-tae dead, that left only two.

He tapped the screen and brought the phone to his ear, remaining silent. The party on the other end held their breath as well. The silence stretched so long Jakyeong was on the verge of terminating the call when an unfamiliar, gravelly baritone broke the line.

[Yi-an?]

When Jakyeong didn't immediately reply, the caller spoke again.

[It's Chairman Kang.]

Jakyeong’s posture locked tight, his grip on the chassis stiffening. Checking that the bedroom door was securely latched, he stepped deeper into the suite.

"Yes... Good afternoon, Chairman Kang."

[Are you busy? I'm calling to see if you have time today. If you're free, I would like to meet in person.]

Jakyeong hesitated. Has the old man uncovered the breach? Or did Dmitri double-cross him again and flip back to the patriarch's camp? A dozen tactical calculations fired through his mind in a split second.

[Is it inconvenient?]

Steadying his breathing, Jakyeong offered a deferential acceptance. "Not at all, Chairman. I can make time."

Ending the call, he looked out through the glass. The vibrant blue sky from earlier was slowly curdling into a bruised bank of dark storm clouds.

Shaking off the creeping sense of impending doom, he turned toward the door to brief Kang Il-hyun immediately.
